class.name: CharFXTransform
class.brief_description: Controls how an individual character will be displayed in a [RichTextEffect].
class.description: By setting various properties on this object, you can control how individual characters will be displayed in a [RichTextEffect].

method.name: set_glyph_codepoint_novariant
method.description: The same as setting [member glyph_codepoint], but this allows setting a variation selector, which changes how the font renders the character. The actual meaning of the variation depends on the font itself. Any glyph can have any number of variations at the discretion of the font's creator, and so there is no useful way to document what effect this setting has.

members.member: The [RichTextLabel] that this effect is currently drawing for.
The color the character will be drawn with.

The time elapsed since the [RichTextLabel] was added to the scene tree (in seconds). Time stops when the [RichTextLabel] is paused (see [member Node.process_mode]). Resets when the text in the [RichTextLabel] is changed. [b]Note:[/b] Time still passes while the [RichTextLabel] is hidden.

Contains the arguments passed in the opening BBCode tag. By default, arguments are strings; if their contents match a type such as [bool], [int] or [float], they will be converted automatically. Color codes in the form [code]#rrggbb[/code] or [code]#rgb[/code] will be converted to an opaque [Color]. String arguments may not contain spaces, even if they're quoted. If present, quotes will also be present in the final string. For example, the opening BBCode tag [code][example foo=hello bar=true baz=42 color=#ffffff][/code] will map to the following [Dictionary]: [codeblock] {"foo": "hello", "bar": true, "baz": 42, "color": Color(1, 1, 1, 1)} [/codeblock]

[TextServer] RID of the font used to render glyph, this value can be used with [code]TextServer.font_*[/code] methods to retrieve font information. [b]Note:[/b] Read-only. Setting this property won't affect drawing.
The size of the font as it is being rendered for this specific character. [b]Note:[/b] Read-only. Setting this property won't affect drawing.
Number of glyphs in the grapheme cluster. This value is set in the first glyph of a cluster. [b]Note:[/b] Read-only. Setting this property won't affect drawing.
Glyph flags. See [enum TextServer.GraphemeFlag] for more info. [b]Note:[/b] Read-only. Setting this property won't affect drawing.

Glyph index specific to the [member font]. If you want to replace this glyph, use [method TextServer.font_get_glyph_index] with [member font] to get a new glyph index for a single character. Consider using [member glyph_codepoint] for convenience, which allows inputting a Unicode codepoint. In C# environments, the [code]System.Text.Rune[/code] struct is especially useful for this purpose (cast to [code]uint[/code]).

Unicode codepoint of this character as it appears in the text. [b]Note that this does not support compound Unicode characters, and so complex joined characters, such as flag emojis, will not be affected.[/b] In C# environments, the [code]System.Text.Rune[/code] struct is especially useful for this purpose. Changing this value will change the value of [member glyph_index] automatically. Returns [code]-1[/code] if the font or font size is invalid and thus getting a codepoint is impossible.
The position offset the character will be drawn with (in pixels).
If [code]true[/code], FX transform is called for outline drawing. [b]Note:[/b] Read-only. Setting this property won't affect drawing.
Absolute character range in the string, corresponding to the glyph. [b]Note:[/b] Read-only. Setting this property won't affect drawing.
The character offset of the glyph, relative to the current [RichTextEffect] custom block. [b]Note:[/b] Read-only. Setting this property won't affect drawing.

The current transform of the current glyph. It can be overridden (for example, by driving the position and rotation from a curve). You can also alter the existing value to apply transforms on top of other effects.
If [code]true[/code], the character will be drawn. If [code]false[/code], the character will be hidden. This will not cause text to reflow, leaving a gap in the character's place.
